classes.name: General Elections (National Assembly)
classes.locator: https://gecom.org.gy/public/uploads/laws/Cap_103_Representation_of_the_People.pdf (s. 11A: at least 65 members by list PR, largest remainder with the Hare quota; 25 from the ten geographical constituencies)
classes.note: Closed-list PR. From 1964 to 1997 a single national list (53 seats; 1980-1997 plus 12 indirectly elected members, class assembly_indirect). Since 2001, 25 seats in the ten regions as geographical constituencies and 40 national top-up seats allocated to make the result proportional nationally: 11 list allocations per election. The 1964 House of Assembly became the first National Assembly at independence in 1966.

classes.name: Election of President
classes.locator: https://gecom.org.gy/public/uploads/laws/Cap_101_Constitution.pdf (art. 177(2): the presidential candidate of the list with the most votes is deemed elected)
classes.note: Executive presidency since the 1980 constitution. Each National Assembly list names its presidential candidate, and a vote for a list counts as a vote for that candidate.
classes.disposition_reason: There is no separate presidential ballot or count: the president is the candidate of the list with the most National Assembly votes (art. 177), so the votes are those of the national_assembly class.

classes.name: Election of President by the National Assembly
classes.name_en: President chosen by the National Assembly
classes.note: Under the republican constitution of 1970 the non-executive president was elected by the National Assembly (1970 and 1976), until the 1980 constitution made the presidency executive and popularly elected.
classes.disposition_reason: The Assembly's votes sit in the Hansard of 1970 and 1976, which the Parliament's site does not publish for those years; no other official record of the count is online.

classes.name: Members of the National Assembly elected by the Regional Democratic Councils and the National Congress of Local Democratic Organs
classes.name_en: National Assembly members elected by regional councils
classes.note: From 1980 to 2001 each of the ten Regional Democratic Councils elected one member and the National Congress of Local Democratic Organs two, beside the 53 list members; the 2000-2001 reforms (Act 4 of 2001) made all 65 seats directly elected.
classes.disposition_reason: The councils' and the Congress's votes were never published by the Elections Commission and no official record is online.

classes.name: Election of the Speaker of the National Assembly
classes.locator: https://gecom.org.gy/public/uploads/laws/Cap_101_Constitution.pdf (art. 56(1): the Assembly elects a Speaker when it first meets after a dissolution)
classes.note: Elected by the members at the first sitting of each Parliament, from members or non-members (art. 56(2)).

classes.name: Referendum on a Bill to alter the Constitution
classes.locator: https://gecom.org.gy/public/uploads/laws/Cap_101_Constitution.pdf (art. 164(2): Bills altering the entrenched articles go to the electors)
classes.note: Held once, on 10 July 1978, on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill that removed the referendum requirement for the new constitution and postponed the elections due that year.
classes.disposition_reason: The Elections Commission's archive starts in 2011 and no official count of the 1978 referendum is online.

classes.name: House of Assembly (1953), Legislative Council (1957), and Legislative Assembly (1961) of British Guiana
classes.note: Universal adult suffrage from 1953, first past the post in single-member constituencies: 24 elected members in 1953, 14 in 1957, and 35 in 1961.
classes.disposition_reason: The official returns sit in the colonial Official Gazette and the reports of the Supervisor of Elections, neither of which is online from an official host.

classes.name: Court of Policy, Combined Court, and Legislative Council of British Guiana (restricted franchise)
classes.note: Elected members on a property and income franchise: eight in the Court of Policy until 1928, then the elected members of the Legislative Council (1928-1953).
classes.disposition_reason: Returns survive only in the colonial Official Gazette and blue books, which no official host publishes online.

classes.name: Judiciary
classes.locator: https://gecom.org.gy/public/uploads/laws/Cap_101_Constitution.pdf (arts. 127-128: judges are appointed by the President)
classes.disposition_reason: No judicial office is elected; the Chancellor and Chief Justice are appointed by the President and the other judges on the advice of the Judicial Service Commission (arts. 127-128).

classes.name: Selection of lists of candidates
classes.disposition_reason: No state-run primary exists: parties submit their lists of candidates to the Chief Election Officer on Nomination Day (Representation of the People Act, ss. 11-11C) and choose them internally.

classes.name: Election of the Executive of the National Toshaos Council
classes.note: The National Toshaos Council of all village Toshaos elects an executive of 20 Toshaos (two per region) and its officers every three years, under the Amerindian Act 2006.
classes.disposition_reason: The council's votes are announced at its conference and reported only in news releases; no official count is published.

classes.name: Regional Elections (Regional Democratic Councils)
classes.locator: https://gecom.org.gy/public/uploads/laws/Cap_28.09_Local_Democratic_Organs.pdf (Regional Democratic Councils Order, para. 5: 15 to 35 members per region, 205 in all)
classes.note: Each of the ten regional councils is elected by closed-list PR (Hare quota, largest remainder) on the same day and ballot paper as the National Assembly.

classes.name: Election of the Regional Chairman and Vice-Chairman
classes.note: Each regional council elects its chairman and vice-chairman from its members at its first meeting.
classes.disposition_reason: The councils' votes are recorded only in their own minutes; no official publication gathers them.

classes.name: Local Government Elections (Municipalities)
classes.finest_note: constituency candidate votes and area-wide list votes (Form 31)
classes.locator: https://gecom.org.gy/public/uploads/laws/Cap_28.03.pdf (s. 38A: mixed system, half the seats by PR on party or voluntary-group lists and half in single-member constituencies)
classes.note: Ten municipalities since 2018 (nine in 2016; Mahdia became a town before the 2018 elections), 154 councillors and 78 constituencies in 2023. Each council has a PR component over the whole area and a first-past-the-post contest in each constituency; GECOM's Form 31 declarations give list votes per area and candidate votes per constituency.

classes.name: Election of Mayors, Deputy Mayors, and NDC Chairpersons
classes.note: Each municipal council elects a mayor and deputy mayor, and each NDC a chairperson and vice-chairperson, from its councillors.
classes.disposition_reason: The councils' votes are recorded only in their minutes; neither GECOM nor the ministry publishes them.

classes.name: Village Council Elections (Toshaos and Councillors)
classes.note: Over 200 titled Amerindian villages elect a Toshao and village councillors every three years under the Amerindian Act 2006 (Cap. 29:01), by secret ballot run by each village with the Ministry of Amerindian Affairs; the 2018 round ran from 15 May to 15 June.

cadence.administered_by: Village returning officers under the Ministry of Amerindian Affairs
cadence.locator: https://dpi.gov.gy/indigenous-village-elections-set-for-may-15/ (These elections are held every three years)

classes.disposition_reason: Each village's returning officer declares its own result; the ministry publishes only lists of new Toshaos in news releases, with no votes, and no official compilation exists.
